title: Market Chorus: model behavior correlation lab for latency, cost, and fidelity
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Objective: build an internal experiment and analytics workspace (the "Market Chorus") that systematically correlates model behavioral signals (latency, token cost, quality/fidelity regressions, hallucination indicators, and stability across prompts) across public providers, open models, and Redwood-hosted variants.

Rationale: existing model scouting artifacts capture snapshots of capability or price; we lack a cross-dimensional, time-series correlate that surfaces when a model's latency/cost tradeoff starts to degrade relative to fidelity for key customer workloads. This makes it hard to prioritize model rollouts, quantized fallbacks, or procurement triggers for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope: instrument candidate models (3 open model families + top 5 hosted provider variants) across three synthetic workload classes (short chat, long-context summarization, embedding-indexing) and two regions (us-west-1, eu-west-1). Collect per-request telemetry, cost estimates, and automatic quality proxies (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, LM-based hallucination heuristics, and rerank agreement). Produce a correlation dashboard and a short decision rubric for PM/Eng to act on (fallback, reserve procurement, or pursue quantization).
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry pipeline ingests model request-level metrics for latency, token counts, and cost estimates for each target model and region
Quality proxies automatically computed for the three workload classes and stored as time-series (minutely/hourly)
Dashboard visualizing pairwise correlations (latency vs fidelity, cost vs hallucination score) with filters for region/model/version
Short decision rubric (PDF) summarizing triggers for: reserve Dedicated capacity, enable quantized fallback, or flag for onboarding replacement
Writeup with sample customer-impact vignettes and one recommended runbook for an enterprise facing a 40% latency regression
deliverables: Market Chorus telemetry workbook (time-series dataset in S3)
Grafana/Looker dashboard linked from Console -> Signals
PM decision rubric (Confluence) and 4-slide stakeholder brief
Prototype playbook for automatic fallback rules mapped to signal thresholds
updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff with Applied ML and Infra. Agreed telemetry schema and provisional sampling rate (1% of synthetic requests, 100 qps burstcap for probes).
2025-02-25: Infra stubbed ingestion path; added cost estimator to runtime metrics. Need ENG to add hallucination proxy endpoint. Assigned ENG-31245 to eng-telemetry team.

2025-03-01: Pilot run completed for 'short chat' workloads in us-west-1. Early signal: one open model family shows stable fidelity but 25% higher tail latency under batching; engineering to triage kernel selection impact.
2025-03-07: First dashboard draft in Looker ready for review. PM/Design sync scheduled 2025-03-10 to align visualization and decision UI.
comments: Samir Patel (2025-02-20): Prioritize adding a per-request model-variant tag so we can detect soft rollouts.
Iris Moreno (Applied ML, 2025-02-26): Proposed hallucination proxy using ensemble agreement + entity hallucination count. Will prototype by 2025-03-04.
Evan Brooks (Infra, 2025-03-02): Noted that eu-west ingestion will need additional egress budget; asked PM to estimate run duration for cost approval.
decision: We will prioritize building the correlation pipeline and dashboard before a full procurement playbook. If the lab finds >30% cost-per-quality degradation for a model that a top-20 enterprise uses, we trigger a follow-up project to negotiate vendor SLAs or scope Dedicated capacity experiments.
tradeoffs: Sampling rate vs cost: higher sampling gives finer signal but increases egress and compute costs; decided on staged ramp from 0.5% -> 2% based on early run feedback
Synthetic vs customer workloads: synthetic probes accelerate iteration but may miss edge-case regressions; plan to add two customer-supplied prompt-sets for higher-fidelity validation in phase 2
Short-term observability vs long-term instrumentation: a quick Looker-based dashboard is acceptable now but invest in persistent metric schema for future automated alerts
risks: Bias in quality proxies: automatic hallucination heuristics may under/over-index certain domains leading to false triggers
Egress/cost overruns when scaling probes across regions without approvals
Model vendor rate limits or billing constraints could throttle probes and produce noisy latency signals
next_steps: Infra to merge ingestion schema PR and open ENG-31245 for tagging changes by 2025-03-06
Design & PM review dashboard draft on 2025-03-10 and fold feedback into v1
Run phase-1 swept experiments in eu-west-1 for all workload classes during week of 2025-03-17
